question: A current carrying wire is placed horizontally in a magnetic field with north pole in upward and south pole in downward direction. The wire is deflected towards south direction. The direction of electrons in the wire is:
solution:
The correct answer is __west to east.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a **current-carrying wire is placed in a magnetic field**, a force is exerted on it due to the interaction between the magnetic field and the current.
 
• This force is perpendicular to both the magnetic field and the current direction and is given by the **right-hand rule**.
 
• Since the north pole of the magnet is facing upwards, the force direction is reversed due to the negative charge of electrons in the wire, which results in the wire deflecting towards the south direction.
 
• The electrons are flowing from **west to east.**
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/db02749044689370143951d12e1c574f50f296ef6aef76c54f0cb416e6a5b7f1.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Fleming’s Right Hand Thumb Rule:

 
• This rule is frequently applied as a mnemonic to **help remember the way the three axes—X, Y, and Z**—orient on a three-dimensional plane.
 
• It says that when we position our right hand's thumb, forefinger, and middle finger perpendicular to one another, then:
 
 
• The thumb indicates the **direction in which the conductor is moving in relation to the magnetic field**.
 
• The **direction of the magnetic field** is shown by the forefinger.
 
• The middle finger is pointing in the** induced current's direction.**
